title: Private Ecosystem Review preserves the risk gate by moving it into a confidential channel rather than removing it
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.10.7 is the provision that makes the confidentiality framework defensible. "Prior to activation of a Confidential Strategic Integration and Deployment for end user interactions or deposits, Designated Contributors shall confidentially disclose **all relevant deployment details** to the Spark Risk Council, and to applicable Sky ecosystem governance reviewers designated for confidential ecosystem reviews." Reviewers "may object to a deployment where they identify concerns within the scope of their review authority," and on objection "Designated Contributors **shall not activate** the deployment for end user interactions or deposits until the identified concerns have been resolved, any required approvals have been obtained, or the deployment has otherwise been cancelled and wound down."

The distinction being drawn is between secrecy from the *public* and secrecy from *reviewers*. A partner's NDA is a commercial requirement about announcement timing; it is not a reason for a deployment holding user funds to escape risk review. So the framework keeps the review and changes only its audience.

Structurally this preserves the Spark Risk Council's core power — the pre-activation veto established at A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4 — inside a channel where public disclosure is impossible. Confidential activity is thereby subject to the same gate as a public Root Edit proposal, with the same body deciding, just without the forum thread.

It also supplies the missing protection for users identified in the framework's risk allocation. Depositors into an undisclosed deployment cannot exercise informed consent; the reviewers exercise it on their behalf, and the trigger is precisely "end user interactions or deposits" — the moment third-party money becomes reachable.

Two limits are worth stating. The objection power is bounded to "concerns within the scope of their review authority," so it inherits the SRC's enumerated scope rather than becoming a general veto. And the same appointment dependency applies: the body protecting users here is appointed, paid and removable by the Spark Foundation, which is the sole Designated Contributor whose deployments it reviews.
